hp.details: Broken Threshold 75 — it crazes as it loses HP, and is Destroyed at 0 HP. Shatter it and the way back shatters with it (see The Way Back).

stealth.details: (no roll — it is the looking-glass the party stepped through, in plain view by the hall's entrance)

details.description: A tall looking-glass in a frame of dull silver, standing by the entrance to the Hall of Reflections — the twin of the Glass to the Ice Palace, and the pane the party stepped through to cross into the Shadow Plane. Its surface keeps each reflection a half-beat too long. Unlike the Queen's mirror, no rime bleeds through it: the killing cold does not gather here, and the floor before it stays bare.
details.disable:
It is an object: Hardness 14 (halved to 7 against adamantine), HP 150, Broken Threshold 75; attacks resolve against AC 33. It can be defaced with @Check[thievery|dc:38|name:Deface the Glass] or simply battered apart. It carries no Queen's Rime, so there is no channel to sever — harming it is purely a matter of breaking glass.

Broken (75 HP): the pane spiderwebs and the reflections splinter, but it holds — and still works as a doorway.

Destroyed (0 HP): the glass shatters and the way back to the waking world goes with it. Anyone still in the Shadow Plane is trapped in this hall and must find another path out (see The Way Back).

description.value: This looking-glass is the doorway the party stepped through — their one route back to the waking world. Cracked or Broken, it still serves; but if it is Destroyed (reduced to 0 Hit Points) the pane shatters and the doorway closes. Anyone still in the Shadow Plane is trapped in the Hall of Reflections, with no way back through this glass — they must press on to the Glass to the Ice Palace or find another path out. Make sure the players grasp what they are smashing before they commit to it.
